From: Amanda Chen <amanda@atlashealth.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Observability handoff & SLOs for AtlasHealth integration

Hi Connor / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to lock down observability responsibilities and an initial SLO matrix before we switch traffic for our pilot on 2026-11-01. High-level asks:

- Shared dashboard for 3 core flows (ingest, inference, reranking)
- Tracing hooks for cross-service spans (frontend -> api-gateway -> inference)
- Error taxonomy so our on-call knows what to page vs what to monitor in dashboards
- A short runbook for failover and rollback steps (first responders: Atlas SRE + Redwood CS)

Can you propose a short mutual action plan + owners? We're time-boxed on the pilot date, so a simple, testable handoff would be ideal.

Also, we can make the staging Grafana/Datadog accounts available if that helps.

— Amanda
Amanda Chen
Platform Engineering Lead | AtlasHealth

Amanda — thanks for the clear ask. I've sketched a lightweight action plan below and attached a first-pass telemetry playbook + SLO matrix. Please review and tell us which items Atlas wants to own vs. Redwood.

Proposed 2-week ramp (summary):
1) Today–Oct 9: Align owners and grant access to staging dashboards (owner: Atlas SRE + Redwood CS).
2) Oct 10–16: Instrument tracing hooks and validate spans end-to-end (owner: Redwood Eng; verification: Atlas test harness).
3) Oct 17–23: Wire dashboards & alerts, runbook draft and tabletop exercise (owner: Redwood CS + Atlas SRE).
4) Oct 24–30: Stabilization window, remediate gaps, finalize runbook and on-call rotation for pilot.

Quick asks for Atlas so we can move immediately: staging Grafana/DG credentials, expected QPS/99th percentile latencies for inference, and any current error codes you already classify as critical.

Attachments: telemetry-playbook-draft.pdf, SLO-matrix-AtlasHealth.xlsx

I'll set up a 30-min checkpoint tomorrow to walk through the playbook.

Thanks — Connor

- Dashboard scope: we recommend 6 tiles per flow (traffic, latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, saturation, queue length, recent traces link). We'll template these for Grafana and Datadog.
- Alert routing: critical pages to Atlas SRE pager; degraded-but-not-blocking to Redwood CS Slack channel #atlas-ops + email.
- Runbook template: include quick triage checklist, common remediation commands, and the rollback matrix (API key rotation, model pin fallback).

Forwarding some implementation notes from infra/serving runtime for the tracing hooks and error taxonomy. This is intentionally terse so your SRE can paste into their codebase.

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Amanda — thanks for the clear ask. I've sketched a lightweight action plan below and attached a first-pass telemetry playbook + SLO matrix. Please review and tell us which items Atlas wants to own vs. Redwood.

Notes:
- Tracing: add client span at frontend with tags {request_id, user_tier, model_variant}. Redwood SDK will propagate x-redwood-trace-id and merge with gateway spans. Expected change: add one extra 2–3KB header; no payload change.
- Sampling: 5% global + 100% for errors (status >= 500) during ramp window.
- KV cache visibility: emit cache_hit/cache_miss metrics per model_id to avoid noisy p95s.
- Error taxonomy suggestion: map infra timeouts -> "inference_timeouts", model OoM -> "model_failures", upstream 4xx -> "client_errors". We'll provide a short mapping table for your SRE.
- Runtime hooks: example instrumentation path: frontend -> proxy -> model-host. We will add a helper in the SDK for attaching span links.

I'll drop a short runbook stub into the Drive folder (runbook-template.md).

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: runbook-template.md (text/markdown)]
